web_evidence.title: Hawaii: A Novel — ebook preview
web_evidence.note: The sustained opening initially presents geological and human events externally but twice exposes the teller as I, including retrospective reference to what he previously narrated; this establishes a personal controlling voice locally.

web_evidence.title: The Second-Greatest Stories Ever Told: Middlebrow Epic
web_evidence.note: Tom Perrin's scholarly structural analysis traces increasingly personal intrusions across the novel and explains that the ending reveals the narrator as story participant Hoxworth Hale.

web_evidence.title: Figuring Futures: Early Asian American Mixed-Race Literature
web_evidence.note: Melissa Eriko Poulsen's UC Santa Cruz literature dissertation identifies Hoxworth Hale as Hawaii's narrator while analyzing the novel's complete Golden Men structure.

web_evidence.title: Hawaii Part 6 Summary & Analysis
web_evidence.note: The Part 6 analysis explicitly states that the conclusion reveals Hoxworth Hale to have narrated the entire book and discusses him speaking as narrator.

web_evidence.title: Hawaii Analysis
web_evidence.note: The style analysis independently identifies Hoxworth Hale, a character within the novel, as its narrator.

person_note: The controlling teller is Hoxworth Hale, a character who participates in the novel and is explicitly revealed at the end as narrator of the entire book. Much of the prose, including the long Kamejiro quotation, uses omniscient-looking third-person presentation, but the authorized opening already contains the teller's I, and scholarly whole-book analysis traces further personal intrusions before Hale's identification. Under the task's participation-based definition, these are modes used by one first-person narrator, not sustained autonomous sections controlled by different narrators, so FIRST is preferable to ALTERNATING. The main residual peculiarity is Hale's implausibly broad access to events long before his lifetime, but that affects narratorial reliability and convention rather than his disclosed participation.
